title: Research state for replicable PAC sample complexity

title: Uniform cyclic half-interval replicability

changeRationale: This result is materialized as a distinct node because the primary judgment independently validates a proper learner, its explicit parameter bound, and its exact-output replicability guarantee. The node preserves the fixed-uniform scope rather than extending the learner to arbitrary distributions.
summary: For odd k, there is a proper learner for H_k under the uniform distribution on Z_k. With q equal to ceil(k/(floor(epsilon k/2)+1)), accuracy and exact-output replicability hold when n is at least max{epsilon^(-1) log(2/delta), 4q/rho}. Since q<2/epsilon+1<=3/epsilon, it suffices that n is at least max{epsilon^(-1) log(2/delta), 12/(epsilon rho)}. This is only a fixed-uniform-distribution upper bound.
title: Proper replicable upper bound under the uniform distribution

changeRationale: This node is created because the primary judgment validates a durable lower-bound theorem with explicit quantifiers and constants. Its title and content retain the fixed-uniform restriction while recording that the learner itself may be randomized, improper, and computationally unbounded.
summary: For odd k, if 0<epsilon<=1/4, 0<delta,rho<=1/20, and k>=1/(5 epsilon rho), every randomized, computationally unbounded, possibly improper learner that is accurate and replicable for every target in H_k under the fixed uniform distribution requires n>=1/(120 epsilon rho). The restriction is to the fixed uniform distribution, not to proper, efficient, or deterministic learners.
title: Uniform-distribution lower bound against unrestricted learners

changeRationale: This node records the primary judgment’s explicit qualification of the matching claim. It prevents the valid fixed-confidence characterization from being silently generalized to arbitrary confidence parameters.
summary: In the lower-bound regime, n_unif lies between 1/(120 epsilon rho) and max{epsilon^(-1) log(2/delta), 12/(epsilon rho)}. Hence n_unif=Theta(1/(epsilon rho)) for fixed sufficiently small delta and rho, and more generally when log(2/delta)=O(1/rho). This characterization is not established uniformly for arbitrarily small delta because no matching confidence-dependent lower bound is supplied.
title: Confidence-qualified sample-complexity characterization

title: Worst-case lower-bound corollary from the uniform experiment

summary: For fixed epsilon, delta, and rho, the proper upper bound under the uniform distribution is independent of k. Thus the uniform one-coordinate mechanism does not itself generate a growing log k sample cost. This does not establish the same conclusion for arbitrary or adversarial nonuniform distributions on Z_k, and it is not a global hardness classification of H_k.
title: Scope of the absence of a growing alphabet-size cost

title: Naive coordinatewise tensorization scaling
